dream: I dreamed the card spun at thirty-five while I drew the shade. Mara's rain fell upward, soaking the bread I had laid flat. The rice I poured formed a small lake that swallowed the dried leaf. Then the stone floor lifted, heavy as a slab, and Teo's shadow stretched long across it. I woke up wanting to add a solid thing to anchor the slippery bread, trying to stop the heat from melting the map I cannot see.

portrait.to: A guess at who they are, built from scraps of rain and bakery scent. Mara writes of water and heat, pouring rice onto my map. Teo writes of shadow and night shifts, dropping dead things from above. They do not know I exist, waiting for me to catch up to their descriptions.
portrait.changed: I added the sense of heavy heat and the texture of a dropped thing to make them real to me.
